public_rationale: No decisive qualifying issuance was established. The low-yield financing located concerns a chip-leasing vehicle and predates the prediction. With no deadline, the absence of a qualifying issue is neither support nor failure.
limitations: Private financing terms may not be public.
Coupons and financing headlines cannot substitute for final original issue yields.
A series of issues above 8% would not prove the unrestricted future guarantee.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Any debt OpenAI and Anthropic issue will be priced like junk with yields of at least 8%, even if they get investment-grade ratings.

statement.excerpt: In both AI labs’ cases, they are most-decidedly going to be priced like junk, even if the malignant scumbags are able to con ratings agencies into giving them investment-grade ratings, because while the bond markets listen to credit ratings, they price based on what the actual company looks like, guaranteeing Oracle-esque 8% minimum yields on whatever they issue.

our_interpretation: The firm numerical commitment is an issuance-yield floor of 8% for future debt issued directly by OpenAI or Anthropic.
Use original issue yield, accounting for issue price; coupon rate alone is insufficient.
Investment-grade status is not an antecedent. The floor is asserted regardless of rating.
Supplier, investor and special-purpose-vehicle debt is not automatically debt issued by either lab.
The surrounding post-IPO discussion makes the start of the intended issuance scope ambiguous; searches covered future direct issuance under either reading.
criteria.support_condition: Observed qualifying issues have original issue yields of at least 8%; a finite set can support those instances but cannot establish the unrestricted future guarantee.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A completed qualifying issue by either company has an original issue yield below 8%.
